profile.reading: Pearl Plaza Office Building sits at 601 East 18th Avenue in the North Capitol Hill neighborhood of Denver, Colorado, immediately east of the state capitol. Public address records identify the occupant of the building as the Colorado Governor's Office of Information Technology (OIT), the state agency that runs shared computing and network infrastructure for Colorado state government. The building is a modest three story commercial office structure, not a purpose built or converted data center. It appears in this registry because an OpenStreetMap contributor tagged it with a CLLI code, a type of location identifier the telecommunications industry assigns to central offices and other facilities that carry telecom equipment, together with a general data center tag. That combination most plausibly reflects a telecom equipment room or network point of presence serving the tenants of the building and the state IT operations housed there, rather than a wholesale or retail colocation facility open to outside customers. No square footage, power capacity, or other data center specification is published for this address, because none applies to what public records indicate is a government office building rather than a dedicated data center.

reading.body:
Pearl Plaza Office Building is a state government office building in Denver, not a data center, and it should be excluded from any count of Colorado AI capacity.

The building at 601 East 18th Avenue houses the Colorado Governor's Office of Information Technology, the agency running shared computing and network infrastructure for state government. It entered the registry because an OpenStreetMap contributor tagged it with a CLLI code, a telecom industry location identifier, alongside a general data center tag. That combination points to a telecom equipment room or network point of presence serving the building's tenants, not a facility open to outside customers.

The distinction matters because grid constraint analysis depends on which buildings actually draw large loads. A three story office structure with no published power capacity adds nothing to that picture. Colorado has 17 mapped facilities, and only 3 publish power specifications, totaling 26.35 MW. This address is not among those three.

What the data does not provide is any capacity figure for this site, because none exists to publish. It also does not establish how much power the state IT operations inside the building consume. The record covers a tagging artifact and its correction, not a measured load.
